sub_answers.sub_question: Obstructions to existence of nontrivial derivations preserving the twisting map in Hom-algebras
sub_answers.text: The definition and study of α^kβ^l-generalized derivations and α^kβ^l-quasi-derivations indicate that derivations must be adapted to commute appropriately with the twisting maps, which constrains existence of nontrivial derivations preserving the twist [d46845s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Known classification difficulties or counterexamples showing failure of PBW or envelope constructions in Hom-contexts
Limitations of standard cohomology theories to detect deformations or extensions of Hom-algebras
sub_answers.text: Cohomology theories must be adapted to Hom-structures to encode generalized derivation extensions and deformations, showing that standard (classical) cohomology is inadequate without modification [d66753s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Issues in defining and classifying fiberwise Hom-structures on bundles or sheaves over base spaces
sub_answers.text: Classification of fiberwise Hom-structures on bundles involves adapting extension and T*-extension techniques, and T*-extensions provide a method for realizing finite-dimensional nilpotent metric Hom-Nambu-Lie superalgebras under surjectivity of the twisting map α [d21442s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Open problems and conjectures concerning rigidity, integrability, or classification of affine-twisted Hom-algebras
sub_answers.text: Cohomological obstructions to extensions and the necessity of tailored Hom-cohomology theories leave classification and rigidity questions unresolved for many Hom-type algebras [d39985s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Description of modules and representations of Hom-Lie algebras and changes from classical representation theory
sub_answers.text: Representations of Hom-type algebras are defined in parallel with classical notions and include modules and cohomology theories adapted to the Hom-structure [d46845s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Characterization of derivation algebras (inner versus outer derivations) in Hom-type algebras
sub_answers.text: Hom-type and BiHom-type theories introduce generalized derivations such as α^kβ^l-generalized derivations, α^kβ^l-quasi-derivations and α^kβ^l-quasi-centroids adapted to the twisting maps [d46845s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Use of Hom-pre-Lie structures in deformation theory and explicit deformation formulas
sub_answers.text: Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras are developed within a Hom-Lie cohomology framework and relate to Manin triples and matched pairs, providing a structure controlling deformations in the Hom setting [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Role of Hom-algebra structures in geometry: connections to affine manifolds, flat connections, and fibers
sub_answers.text: Hom-type algebraic structures interact with affine and statistical geometry through affine connections and their geodesic properties, and geodesic connectedness of affine connections can follow from geodesic completeness in specific statistical manifolds [d106337s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Examples where twisting produces new Lie algebra actions or altered symmetry algebras in physical models
sub_answers.text: Twisting by self-morphisms produces Hom-versions of classical algebras and closes the category under such twistings, thereby producing new algebraic actions and modified symmetry algebras [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Definition and axioms of a Hom-Lie algebra including the twisting map and Hom-Jacobi identity
sub_answers.text: A Hom-Lie algebra is a twisted generalization of a Lie algebra that includes a linear twisting map acting on the underlying vector space [d9858s0p0]. A Hom-Lie algebra satisfies a Hom-Jacobi identity in which the classical Jacobi identity is modified by the twisting map [d9858s0p0]. The category of Hom-Lie algebras is closed under twisting by self-morphisms, yielding new Hom-Lie algebras from existing ones via such twists [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Definition and axioms of a pre-Lie algebra (left-symmetric algebra) and its relation to Lie algebras
sub_answers.text: A pre-Lie algebra, also called a left-symmetric algebra, is an algebraic structure whose product is not necessarily associative but satisfies a left-symmetry identity relating associators [d52442s0p0]. Pre-Lie algebras are interconnected with Lie algebras through skew-symmetrization of the pre-Lie product, which produces a Lie bracket [d52442s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Definition and construction of an affine twist or affine action on an algebraic structure
sub_answers.text: An affine action or affine twist on an algebraic structure refers to an additional affine action or affine datum enriching module-expanded varieties and their extensions [d89275s0p0]. Affine datum and affine actions are used to parametrize and reconstruct extensions in varieties of algebras with multilinear operators [d89275s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Standard examples of Hom-algebras obtained via Yau twist from associative or Lie algebras
sub_answers.text: Standard Hom-algebras can be obtained by twisting classical algebras via self-morphisms, a procedure that constructs Hom-Lie-Yamaguti and Hom-Lie algebras from classical Lie-Yamaguti and Lie algebras respectively [d9858s0p0]. Constructions of Hom-Lie-Yamaguti algebras from classical Lie-Yamaguti algebras and from Malcev algebras are explicitly given as examples of such twists [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Relationship between pre-Lie algebras and their associated Lie algebras via commutator bracket
sub_answers.text: Given a pre-Lie algebra, the commutator bracket obtained by skew-symmetrizing the pre-Lie product defines an associated Lie algebra bracket [d52442s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Formulation of the Hom-Jacobi identity and how it modifies the classical Jacobi identity
sub_answers.text:
Hom-type algebras replace the classical Jacobi identity by a Hom-Jacobi identity that is twisted by a structure self-map (endomorphism) of the algebra [d9858s0p0].
The Hom-Jacobi identity is formulated so that the usual cyclic sum involving the Lie bracket is composed with the twisting map, producing a modified Jacobi condition consistent with the Hom-structure [d9858s0p0].
Categories of Hom-type algebras are closed under twisting by self-morphisms, which implements this modification of the Jacobi identity [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Expression of pre-Lie identity and its Hom-version under a twisting endomorphism
sub_answers.text:
Pre-Lie identities admit Hom-versions by composing the pre-Lie product identities with a twisting endomorphism, yielding Hom-pre-Lie algebra identities formulated in the cohomological framework for Hom-Lie algebras [d55626s0p0].
Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras and their matched-pair formulations use these twisted pre-Lie identities to define algebraic compatibility and bialgebra structures [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Definition of derivations of Hom-algebras and how twisting affects the Leibniz rule
sub_answers.text:
Derivations in BiHom- and Hom-type algebras are generalized to include factors of the twisting maps, e.g. α^kβ^l-generalized derivations and quasi-derivations that record powers of the structure maps in their defining relations [d46845s0p0].
Twisting alters the Leibniz rule by inserting the structure maps into the Leibniz-type identities, producing Hom- or BiHom-Leibniz rules compatible with the twisting maps [d46845s0p0].
Hom-Leibniz bialgebras and related constructions incorporate these twisted derivation notions in their matched-pair and Manin triple equivalences [d70925s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Construction of universal enveloping algebras for Hom-Lie algebras and corresponding PBW-type statements
Cohomology theories for Hom-Lie or Hom-pre-Lie algebras and the role of the twisting map in differentials
sub_answers.text:
Cohomology theories for Hom-Lie and Hom-pre-Lie algebras are developed using adapted cohomology complexes that take the twisting map into account [d55626s0p0].
Twisting maps enter the differential and grading structures of these complexes, and twisting theory using Nijenhuis-Richardson brackets and bidegrees underlies constructions of L-infinity algebras and cohomologies for twisted operators [d87962s0p0].
Cohomologies for symmetric BiHom-Leibniz algebras and for twisted relative operators are explicitly formulated to record the action of the twisting morphisms in cochains and differentials [d46845s0p0][d87962s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What obstructions, cohomology classes, or explicit counterexamples prevent existence of nonzero derivations D on Hom-algebras (A, μ, α) satisfying D∘α = α∘D and the Hom-Leibniz rule; search for results citing specific Hom-Lie, Hom-associative, or multiplicative Hom-algebras where such α-compatible derivations are shown to be trivial or constrained by eigenvalue conditions on α or center-related ideals
sub_answers.text: Inner-derivations and centroids for finite-dimensional complex Hom-associative trialgebras are identified and computed in the literature [d84971s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which published classification failures, explicit counterexamples, or obstruction theorems demonstrate that standard Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt (PBW) theorems or universal enveloping algebra constructions do not hold in Hom-algebra settings (e.g., Hom-Lie, color Hom-Lie, or q-deformed Hom-algebras); list papers exhibiting non-PBW filtered/graded mismatches, necessary extra hypotheses, or invariants that obstruct enveloping algebra existence
sub_answers.text: A categorical criterion for PBW-type theorems states that a natural transformation of monads enjoys a PBW property only if its codomain is a free right module over its domain [d43520s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In what ways do classical cohomology theories (Hochschild, Chevalley–Eilenberg, Harrison) fail to detect nontrivial first- or second-order deformations, extensions, or obstructions in Hom-associative or Hom-Lie algebras; seek specific examples where ordinary cohomology groups vanish while Hom-deformations exist, or where one must modify differential or twisting in cochain complexes to capture Hom-deformation classes
sub_answers.text: Cohomology theory for Hom-Lie algebras is used as the framework to introduce and study Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras and to analyze coboundary Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What technical difficulties, no-go results, or classification gaps arise when attempting to define fiberwise Hom-structures (families of Hom-algebras) on vector bundles, principal bundles, or sheaves over manifolds/schemes; look for literature describing obstruction classes, nonlocality of the twisting map α, failure of local triviality, or incompatibility with transition functions and Čech cocycles
sub_answers.text: A Hom-Lie algebroid structure has been defined on the pullback of the cotangent bundle of a Hom-Poisson manifold, giving an explicit geometric construction of Hom-structures on bundles [d32486s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which open problems, conjectures, or unresolved classification questions are currently stated about rigidity, integrability of infinitesimal Hom-deformations, or complete classification of affine-twisted Hom-algebras (e.g., Hom-analogues of affine Lie algebras, current algebras, or deformations of polynomial algebras twisted by affine maps); include precise formulations, known partial results, and suggested approaches in recent papers
sub_answers.text: Extensions of hom-Lie color algebras are obstructed by a cohomological class: existence of an extendible hom-Lie color algebra requires the triviality of a certain element of the third cohomology [d39985s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe module categories and representation theory for Hom-Lie algebras: define Hom-modules, Hom-representations, cohomology of representations, and compare explicit differences with classical Lie algebra modules (e.g., failure of complete reducibility, modified weight space decompositions, and examples where the module action is twisted by structure maps).
sub_answers.text: Representations and a cohomology theory are defined for symmetric BiHom-Leibniz algebras of type B1, providing a notion of Hom-modules and Hom-representations adapted to the BiHom setting [d46845s0p0]. Cohomology for n-ary multiplicative Hom-Nambu-Lie superalgebras is developed to study representations and extensions, relating extensions to first cohomology groups [d21442s0p0]. Twisting by self-morphisms leads to categories of Hom-type algebras closed under such twists, yielding representation categories related by twisting and untwisting functors in equivariant map algebra settings [d9858s0p0][d10834s0p0]. The use of cohomology theory for Hom-Lie algebras underpins deformation and representation constructions for Hom-pre-Lie and related Hom-algebras [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Classify derivations of Hom-type algebras: give criteria distinguishing inner and outer derivations for Hom-Lie and Hom-associative algebras, compute the derivation algebra in model examples (e.g., q-deformations, Heisenberg-type Hom-Lie algebras), and describe conditions under which all derivations are inner or when nontrivial outer derivations appear.
sub_answers.text: Alpha-type generalized derivations, quasi-derivations and quasi-centroids are defined for (Bi)Hom-Leibniz and colour BiHom-Leibniz algebras, providing criteria to distinguish classes of derivations in Hom-type algebras [d46845s0p0]. Alpha-inner derivations and centroids are identified and computed for finite-dimensional Hom-trialgebras, giving explicit descriptions of inner derivations in model Hom-associative trialgebras [d84971s0p0]. Complete descriptions of derivations are obtained for many algebras of measurable operators, and sufficient conditions are given under which local or 2-local derivations are actual derivations, illustrating when all derivations reduce to inner ones or when outer derivations persist [d31200s0p0][d35042s0p0]. Outer restricted derivations with specified nilpotency properties exist for finite-dimensional nilpotent restricted Lie algebras except in explicit exceptional cases, indicating circumstances where nontrivial outer derivations appear [d10497s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain how Hom-pre-Lie (Hom-left-symmetric) algebra structures control deformations: provide explicit Hochschild/Chevalley–Eilenberg-type deformation complexes for Hom-pre-Lie algebras, write down first-order and higher-order deformation formulas, and give worked examples of formal deformations and obstruction formulas.
sub_answers.text: Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras are introduced within the cohomology framework for Hom-Lie algebras, allowing the study of deformations and coboundary Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras via cohomological methods [d55626s0p0]. Equivalences are established between Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras, standard Manin triples for Hom-pre-Lie algebras, and certain matched pairs, providing algebraic structures that control deformations [d55626s0p0]. Hom-O-operators and Hom-L-dendriform algebras are used to construct Hom-s-matrices which in turn produce Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras, giving explicit tools for building and deforming Hom-pre-Lie structures [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Investigate geometric interpretations of Hom-algebras: relate Hom-Lie and Hom-associative structures to affine and Cartan connections, characterize when a Hom-connection is flat, describe Hom-versions of tangent Lie algebras and Lie algebroids, and give examples tying Hom-structures to fiber bundle geometry.
sub_answers.text: A modified definition of Hom-Lie algebroid and its dual description are given, paralleling classical Lie algebroid results and producing Hom-versions of tangent and algebroid structures [d32486s0p0]. The base manifold of a Hom-Lie bialgebroid carries a Hom-Poisson structure, and the pullback cotangent bundle of a Hom-Poisson manifold admits a Hom-Lie algebroid structure, linking Hom-algebras to geometric fibers and connections [d32486s0p0]. Extensions of hom-Lie color algebras admit geometric interpretations involving covariant exterior derivatives, Chevalley derivatives, curvature and Bianchi identities, which tie Hom-extensions to connection-like geometric data [d39985s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide concrete examples from physics where twisting maps alter symmetry algebras: construct explicit physical models (e.g., twisted current algebras, deformed gauge algebras, sigma models) showing how a Hom-twist produces new Lie-like actions, modified conservation laws, or changed symmetry generators, and compute the resulting altered commutation relations.
sub_answers.text: Ternary q-Virasoro-Witt algebras and their q-deformations carry Hom-Nambu-Lie structures obtained via composition and other constructions, providing explicit deformed symmetry algebras where twisting maps alter algebraic relations [d7442s0p0]. Twisting and untwisting functors for equivariant map algebras relate representations of twisted current and multiloop algebras to untwisted analogues, producing concrete altered commutation structures in twisted loop and equivariant settings [d10834s0p0]. Constructions of Hom-Lie-Yamaguti algebras from classical Lie-Yamaguti and Malcev algebras show how twisting by self-morphisms yields new Lie-like actions and deformed algebraic generators in model examples [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide a precise definition of a Hom-Lie algebra: specify the vector space, bilinear bracket, the twisting linear map (often denoted alpha), and state the Hom-skew-symmetry and Hom-Jacobi identity explicitly; include equivalent formulations and common variations (multiplicative Hom-Lie, regularity, invertible twist) and cite the axioms in algebraic form.
sub_answers.text: A Hom-Lie algebra is a twisted generalization of a Lie algebra given by a vector space equipped with a bilinear bracket and a twisting linear map often denoted by \u03b1.[d9858s0p0] A Hom-Lie algebra satisfies Hom-skew-symmetry and a Hom-Jacobi identity involving the twisting map \u03b1.[d9858s0p0] Variations include multiplicative Hom-Lie algebras where the twist preserves the bracket, regularity or invertible-twist variants where the twisting map is invertible, and further generalizations appear in BiHom and Hom-Leibniz hierarchies that recover Lie algebras when one twist is the identity.[d46845s0p0][d39985s0p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: Give the formal definition of a pre-Lie (left-symmetric) algebra: present the bilinear product satisfying left-symmetry (associator identity), alternative names and grading/finite-dimensional variants, and explain the standard construction that associates a Lie bracket to a pre-Lie product; mention key properties (commutator gives Lie algebra, right vs left pre-Lie) and canonical examples.
sub_answers.text: A pre-Lie (left-symmetric) algebra is an algebra with a bilinear product whose associator is left-symmetric, i.e., the associator satisfies the left-symmetry identity that defines left-symmetric or pre-Lie structures.[d41027s0p0] Alternative names include left-symmetric algebra and Vinberg algebra in various contexts and finite-dimensional or graded variants are commonly considered in the literature.[d41027s0p0] The commutator of the pre-Lie product defines a Lie bracket, producing the associated Lie algebra (the sub-adjacent Lie algebra) from the pre-Lie product.[d41027s0p0][d55626s0p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: Define what is meant by an 'affine twist' or an 'affine action' in the context of algebraic structures: describe constructions where an algebra’s operations are modified by affine maps (linear map plus translation), detail how one twists products by affine endomorphisms, and give exact formulas for the twisted product or action and conditions required for structure preservation.

List and describe standard examples of Hom-algebras produced by Yau twisting: explain the Yau twist procedure (given an algebra and an algebra endomorphism phi produce new Hom-structure), provide explicit examples starting from associative algebras and Lie algebras (matrix algebras, polynomial algebras, sl(2)), and give the resulting Hom-associative and Hom-Lie identities for each example.
sub_answers.text: The Yau twist (composition method) produces Hom-algebras by composing an algebraic product with an algebra endomorphism to obtain a new Hom-structure.[d7442s0p0] Categories of Hom-algebras are closed under twisting by self-morphisms, so starting from classical associative or Lie algebras and a chosen algebra endomorphism one obtains Hom-associative and Hom-Lie examples by this procedure.[d9858s0p0] Explicit constructions using this method are used to produce Hom-Nambu-Lie and other Hom-type algebras from their classical counterparts.[d7442s0p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: Explain in detail the relationship between a pre-Lie algebra and its associated Lie algebra obtained via the commutator bracket: derive the Lie bracket [x,y]=x·y−y·x from the pre-Lie product, prove the Jacobi identity using the pre-Lie associator identity, and discuss when this association is functorial or reversible (existence of left-symmetric structures on given Lie algebras).
sub_answers.text: Given a pre-Lie product \u00b7, the commutator [x,y]=x\u00b7y-y\u00b7x defines the associated Lie bracket of the sub-adjacent Lie algebra.[d41027s0p0] The Jacobi identity for this commutator follows from the pre-Lie left-symmetry (associator) identity, so every pre-Lie algebra gives a Lie algebra via the commutator construction.[d41027s0p0][d55626s0p0] The passage from pre-Lie to Lie is functorial in constructions that respect the pre-Lie product and algebra morphisms, and the question of reversing this association (realizing a Lie algebra as sub-adjacent to a pre-Lie algebra) gives the existence problem for left-symmetric structures on given Lie algebras.[d41027s0p0]

sub_answers.sub_question: Give the precise algebraic statement of the Hom-Jacobi identity for a Hom-Lie algebra (L, [ , ], α), compare it term-by-term with the classical Jacobi identity [x,[y,z]] + [y,[z,x]] + [z,[x,y]] = 0, and explain how inserting the twist map α alters antisymmetry or cyclic sums; include canonical examples where the Hom-Jacobi reduces to the ordinary Jacobi when α = id.
sub_answers.text: Hom-type generalizations replace the classical Jacobi cyclic sum by a twisted cyclic sum involving the structure map α in identities of Hom-Lie type [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Write down the standard pre-Lie (left-symmetric) identity ((x·y)·z − x·(y·z)) − ((y·x)·z − y·(x·z)) = 0 and then formulate the Hom-pre-Lie (Hom-left-symmetric) identity for a product · and twist β (e.g. β((x·y)·β(z)) − β(x·(y·z)) = ...); show the explicit terms where β is applied and give sample computations for typical twisting endomorphisms.
sub_answers.text: Hom-pre-Lie (Hom-left-symmetric) structures and Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras are introduced by twisting the usual pre-Lie identities with an endomorphism β and by using the Hom-Lie cohomology framework to formulate the twisted identities [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Define derivations of a Hom-algebra (A, μ, τ) as linear maps D satisfying a twisted Leibniz rule, state that rule explicitly (e.g. D(μ(x,y)) = μ(D(x),τ(y)) + μ(τ(x),D(y)) or variants), discuss inner versus outer derivations in the Hom-setting, and explain how different placements of the twisting map τ change the Leibniz identity and examples illustrating each convention.
sub_answers.text: Generalized derivations in BiHom-Leibniz and (Bi)Hom-type settings are formulated as α^kβ^l-generalized derivations, α^kβ^l-quasi-derivations and α^kβ^l-quasi-centroids, encoding placements of twisting maps into the Leibniz rule [d46845s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe constructions proposed for universal enveloping algebras U_H(L, [,], α) of a Hom-Lie algebra: specify generators, relations (including relations twisted by α), and the maps from L into U_H; state available PBW-type theorems or counterexamples (graded PBW, filtration-based PBW) and the hypotheses on α (invertible, multiplicative) under which PBW analogues have been proved.
sub_answers.text: Universal constructions for Hom-type algebras and doubles appear via Hom-Lie bialgebroids and Hom-Courant algebroids so that generators and relations are modified by the Hom-structure maps, yielding twisted relations consistent with the Hom-structures [d32486s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List cohomology complexes defined for Hom-Lie and Hom-pre-Lie algebras: give the cochain spaces, the explicit differential formulas showing how the twisting map (α or β) enters (e.g. dφ(x1,...,xn+1)=Σ(−1)^{i+1} α^{n−1}(xi)·φ(...)+... ), compare them with Chevalley–Eilenberg and Hochschild differentials, and summarize results on how α alters cocycle conditions, deformation theory, and obstruction classes.
sub_answers.text: Cohomology theories for Hom-Lie and Hom-pre-Lie type algebras are developed and used as the framework to study Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras, deformational constructions, and coboundary structures [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What obstructions, cohomological classes, or explicit counterexamples prevent the existence of nonzero derivations D on a Hom-algebra (A, μ, α) satisfying D∘α = α∘D and the Hom-Leibniz rule? Include known necessary/sufficient conditions, named obstruction groups (e.g., H^1_Hom), and examples where twisting map invariance fails.
sub_answers.text: A cohomological obstruction to the existence of extensions of hom-Lie color algebras appears as the necessity of a trivial member in the third cohomology group for extendibility [d39985s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Which published results, counterexamples, or no-go theorems demonstrate breakdowns of Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt type theorems or universal enveloping algebra constructions for Hom-Lie or Hom-associative algebras? Cite specific constructions that fail (e.g., graded PBW filtrations, lack of Hopf structure) and papers noting classification obstacles.
sub_answers.text: A categorical necessary condition for a natural transformation of monads to enjoy a Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt property is that the transformation make its codomain a free right module over the domain, providing an obstruction to PBW-type theorems when this freeness fails [d43520s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In what ways do classical Hochschild, Chevalley–Eilenberg, or Gerstenhaber cohomology theories fail to detect infinitesimal deformations, obstructions, or extension classes of Hom-algebras? Give concrete discrepancies, proposed Hom-cohomology replacements, and examples where standard cohomology yields false negatives.
sub_answers.text: A cohomology theory and representations are specifically developed for symmetric BiHom-Leibniz algebras of type B1, indicating that standard cohomologies need adaptation for Hom/BiHom settings [d46845s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What are the technical hurdles and classification pathologies encountered when attempting to define fiberwise Hom-algebra structures on vector bundles, principal bundles, or sheaves (e.g., compatibility of local twisting maps α_x, transition functions, or obstruction classes)? Provide explicit obstruction criteria, examples over base spaces (manifolds, schemes), and references.
sub_answers.text: There exists a Hom-Lie algebroid structure on the pullback of the cotangent bundle of a Hom-Poisson manifold, showing that pullback constructions can realize fiberwise Hom-structures under suitable conditions [d32486s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List precise open problems, conjectures, and known partial results about rigidity, integrability, moduli classification, or deformation quantization of affine-type Hom-algebras (e.g., affine Hom-Lie algebras, Hom-current algebras). Include conjectured classification statements, known rigidity theorems, and explicit families remaining unresolved.
sub_answers.text: Classification results exist for n-dimensional Hom-associative trialgebras with n ≤ 3, providing partial classification and indicating larger-dimension families remain unresolved [d84971s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Precise definitions and classifications of modules/representations of Hom-Lie algebras: what are the standard module notions (representation, admissible module, Hom-module), how do weight spaces, irreducibility, and complete-reducibility change compared with classical Lie representation theory, and what cohomology theories control extensions of Hom-modules?
sub_answers.text:
Representations of Hom-type algebras are defined as module-like actions generalized from the classical case to the Hom-setting, including notions called representations and Hom-modules for Hom-Nambu-Lie and related Hom-algebras [d21442s0p0].
Simple and finite-dimensional simple modules and the category of simple modules are studied for Hom-rings and modules over Hom-rings, yielding classifications of simple Hom-modules analogous to classical simple module theory [d64381s0p0].
Weight modules with finite-dimensional weight spaces occur in the study of Dirac cohomology for Lie-type algebras, with vanishing Dirac cohomology for non-highest-weight simple weight modules, illustrating altered behavior of weight-space criteria in twisted settings [d36776s0p0].
Cohomology theories control extensions of Hom-algebras and Hom-modules, and relations between extensions and first cohomology groups (e.g., Z^1) are established for n-ary multiplicative Hom-Nambu-Lie superalgebras, linking extensions to cohomology classes [d21442s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Structural description of derivation algebras for Hom-type algebras: how are inner derivations characterized (e.g., generated by twisted adjoint actions or commutators with structure map), what are concrete criteria distinguishing inner from outer derivations, and when does Der(Hom-A) split into inner plus outer parts (with examples)?
sub_answers.text:
Generalized derivations for BiHom-type algebras are organized by twisted powers of the structure maps, e.g. α^kβ^l-generalized derivations, α^kβ^l-quasi-derivations, and α^kβ^l-quasi-centroids [d46845s0p0].
Inner derivations in Hom-type contexts are characterized via twisted adjoint-like constructions and commutator formulas involving the Hom-structure maps, reflected by the need to include the structure map powers in the definition of derivations [d46845s0p0].
Criteria distinguishing inner from outer derivations are given by membership in these α^kβ^l-generated subspaces versus failure to be expressible as such twisted adjoint actions, yielding a concrete test based on the twisting powers [d46845s0p0].
Splitting results for derivation algebras into inner plus outer parts are treated in the generalized derivation framework for (Bi)Hom-Leibniz algebras where the decomposition uses the α^kβ^l-graded pieces as examples of such structural splits [d46845s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Explicit role of Hom-pre-Lie (or Hom-left-symmetric) algebra structures in deformation theory: what are the governing deformation complexes and brackets, concrete formulas for first- and higher-order Hom-deformations (formal deformations, Maurer–Cartan equations), and worked examples showing how Hom-pre-Lie data produce deformations of associative/Lie-type structures?
sub_answers.text:
Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras and Hom-O-operators provide algebraic structures that generate Hom-s-matrices and hence control coboundary-type constructions and deformations in the Hom-pre-Lie setting [d55626s0p0].
Cohomology theories adapted to Hom-Lie and Hom-pre-Lie algebras underlie deformation complexes and are used to study coboundary Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras and deformations governed by Hom-type cohomology [d55626s0p0].
Hom-O-operators and Hom-L-dendriform algebras furnish explicit algebraic data that produce Hom-s-matrices and thus yield concrete deformation mechanisms from Hom-pre-Lie data to associated Hom-type associative or Lie structures [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How Hom-algebra structures appear in differential geometry: precise connections between Hom-algebras and geometric objects such as affine manifolds, Hom-connections on vector bundles, conditions for flatness and torsion in Hom-connection frameworks, and implications for holonomy and fiber bundle structures?
sub_answers.text:
Hom-Lie algebroids and Hom-Lie bialgebroids give a differential-geometric incarnation of Hom-algebra structures on manifolds and vector bundles [d32486s0p0].
The base manifold of a Hom-Lie bialgebroid carries a Hom-Poisson structure and the pullback cotangent bundle admits a Hom-Lie algebroid structure, linking Hom-algebra data to Hom-connections and geometric brackets [d32486s0p0].
Constructions of Hom-Courant algebroids and the double of a Hom-Lie bialgebroid show how Hom-structures influence geometric objects like Courant-type doubles, with implications for curvature and related geometric identities in the Hom-setting [d32486s0p0].
Extensions of Hom-Lie color algebras are given geometric interpretations involving covariant exterior derivatives, Chevalley derivatives, curvature, and Bianchi identities adapted to Hom-extensions, which constrain flatness and torsion-like conditions in Hom-connection frameworks [d39985s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Concrete examples from physics and mathematical physics where twisting/Hom-type constructions change symmetry algebras: explicit models (e.g., twisted current algebras, q-deformations, Hom-Lie symmetries in sigma-models or field theories) showing how twisting yields new Lie-algebra actions or modifies conserved charges and symmetry generators
sub_answers.text:
Twisting and Hom-type constructions produce new algebraic structures that alter symmetry algebras in mathematical physics contexts by yielding Hom-type generalizations such as Hom-Lie, Hom-Lie-Yamaguti, and Hom-Malcev algebras via twisting by self-morphisms [d9858s0p0].
Hom-type bialgebra and Hom-pre-Lie constructions (including Hom-s-matrices and Hom-O-operators) provide mechanisms to produce new twisted symmetry actions and modified conserved quantities through their induced brackets and operator maps [d55626s0p0].
Categories of Hom-modules and Hom-representations over Hom-rings provide frameworks to construct novel module-theoretic models of twisted symmetries that can be applied in physical models where underlying algebras are deformed or twisted [d64381s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Give a precise definition of a Hom-Lie algebra (A, [·,·], α), spelling out the role of the twisting linear map α: A → A, the skew-symmetry condition, and the Hom-Jacobi identity in full formula form; include the multiplicativity condition α([x,y]) = [α(x),α(y)] when assumed, and list common equivalent axioms and minimal examples (e.g. one-dimensional and zero brackets).
sub_answers.text: A Hom-Lie algebra is a twisted generalization of a Lie algebra specified by a bilinear bracket together with a linear twisting map α: A→A [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: State the definition of a pre-Lie (left-symmetric) algebra (V, ·), write the left-symmetry identity in explicit associator form ( (x·y)·z − x·(y·z) = (y·x)·z − y·(x·z) ), and explain precisely how a pre-Lie product induces a Lie bracket via the commutator [x,y] = x·y − y·x; give standard examples (vector fields with flat torsion-free connection, rooted tree algebra, matrix algebras with Rota–Baxter operators).
sub_answers.text: Pre-Lie (left-symmetric) algebras are classical algebraic structures that admit Hom-analogues called Hom-pre-Lie algebras, and Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras have been introduced within the cohomology theory for Hom-Lie algebras [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Define what is meant by an affine twist or affine action on an algebraic structure: describe the construction of an affine action of a Lie or associative algebra on a vector space as a semidirect product + translation (g ⋉ V) or as a 1-cocycle twisting (ρ, t) with explicit formulas, explain how one builds a new product/bracket by composing with an affine map (x ↦ φ(x)+v) and list the coherence conditions (cocycle, equivariance) needed for the result to remain an algebra of the same type.
sub_answers.text: Affine-type twisting and actions are realized in Hom-type generalizations by combining algebra endomorphisms with additional translation or cocycle data when forming twisted or semidirect constructions in Hom-algebra theory [d46845s0p0][d32486s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Give the explicit statement of Yau’s twisting procedure: start with an associative algebra (A, μ) or Lie algebra (g, [·,·]) and an algebra endomorphism φ, then define the Hom-algebra structures (A, μ_φ = φ ∘ μ, φ) or (g, [x,y]_φ = φ([x,y]), φ), specify necessary conditions on φ (endomorphism, algebra morphism, invertibility not required), and provide standard concrete examples (matrix algebras with conjugation map, polynomial algebras with degree-shift endomorphisms, and classical Lie algebras twisted by scaling maps).
sub_answers.text: Yau’s twisting procedure produces Hom-type algebras by composing an original product or bracket with an algebra endomorphism φ, yielding Hom-algebra structures such as (A, μ_φ=φ∘μ, φ) or (g, [·,·]_φ=φ([·,·]), φ) when φ is an algebra endomorphism [d9858s0p0][d46845s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe in precise terms how every pre-Lie algebra has an associated (subadjacent) Lie algebra obtained by the commutator bracket [x,y] = x·y − y·x, prove that this bracket satisfies the Jacobi identity using the left-symmetry identity, and discuss the converse directions and structural links (left multiplication operators L_x giving a representation of the Lie algebra, conditions under which a Lie algebra admits a compatible pre-Lie structure, and examples where the pre-Lie structure is unique or non-existent).
sub_answers.text: Every pre-Lie algebra has an associated subadjacent Lie algebra obtained by taking the commutator bracket of the pre-Lie product, and Hom-analogues of these relationships are studied via Hom-pre-Lie and Hom-Lie frameworks [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: State the Hom-Jacobi identity used in Hom-Lie algebra literature; compare it symbol-by-symbol with the classical Jacobi identity [x,[y,z]] + [y,[z,x]] + [z,[x,y]] = 0 and explain concretely which terms acquire the twisting map (α) and how sign/placement changes for α([·,·]) versus [α(·),·].
sub_answers.text: Hom-Lie algebras are twisted generalizations of Lie algebras obtained by inserting a linear twisting map α into the identities of Lie algebras [d9858s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Write the standard pre-Lie (left-symmetric) identity in coordinates: (x·y)·z - x·(y·z) = (y·x)·z - y·(x·z). Then give the Hom-pre-Lie analogue for a Hom-algebra with structure map α, specifying exactly where α is inserted (e.g. α(x)·(y·z) or (x·y)·α(z)) and present alternative conventions found in the literature.
sub_answers.text: The literature on Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras works in the general framework of the cohomology theory for Hom-Lie algebras and formulates Hom-pre-Lie algebra identities by inserting the structure map α into the standard pre-Lie identities to obtain Hom-analogues [d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Provide the definition of a derivation D on a Hom-associative or Hom-Lie algebra (A,·,α) including degree-0 and degree-k cases, and show the modified Leibniz rule: D(x·y) = D(x)·α^m(y) + α^n(x)·D(y) (state appropriate m,n), explaining how the twisting map α alters the usual Leibniz identity and examples of inner versus outer Hom-derivations.
sub_answers.text: Works on (Bi)Hom- and Hom-type algebras define generalized derivations such as α^kβ^l-generalized derivations and α-inner derivations, showing that derivation concepts are modified by powers of the twisting maps [d46845s0p0][d84971s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Describe constructions proposed for a universal enveloping algebra U_H(L) of a Hom-Lie algebra (L,[,],α): the generators, relations that encode the Hom-bracket and twisting, and state any Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt-type results or counterexamples (conditions on α such as invertibility or multiplicativity) that ensure a PBW basis exists.
sub_answers.text: Constructions of Hom-Lie-Yamaguti and other Hom-type algebras from classical algebras proceed by twisting classical generators and relations via self-morphisms, which is the method used to build Hom-versions of universal enveloping–type constructions by encoding the bracket and twisting in the relations [d9858s0p0][d55626s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: List cohomology theories defined for Hom-Lie and Hom-pre-Lie algebras (e.g. Chevalley–Eilenberg type, Hochschild-like for Hom-associative), give the differential formula d^p including explicit α-insertions, and explain how the twisting map α changes coboundary operators, cohomology groups, and deformation/extension classification.
sub_answers.text: Cohomology theories for Hom-type algebras include a cohomology theory for Hom-Lie algebras used to study Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras and to analyze coboundary Hom-pre-Lie bialgebras, and these theories incorporate α-insertions into differentials and coboundary operators to classify deformations and extensions [d55626s0p0].
